I'll start by loading the required skills and orienting myself.

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/references

`references/` is a **shared library at the workspace root** — one library for
every project — holding the original source material a blueprint is formalised
from (papers, books, notes). It is indexed by `references/manifest.yaml`. Per-
project files live under each project's directory; `references/` does not — it is
always at the workspace root, and `references/**` is writable from any agent.

A blueprint node derived from a source carries a `\source{...}` anchor. Those
anchors are the audit trail from a formal statement back to where it came from,
so they must be **true**, not plausible.

## The one rule: read before you cite

**Never add a `\source{...}` anchor to a source you have not actually read.** Do
not infer a citation from a title, a topic, a theorem number, or your own prior
knowledge of the result. An anchor asserts "this exact statement/proof appears
here" — if you haven't opened the referenced material and confirmed it, you don't
know that, and a wrong anchor is worse than none (it sends the next reader/agent
to the wrong place and launders a guess as provenance).

Concretely, before writing `\source{...}`:
1. Confirm the source exists in `references/manifest.yaml`. If it isn't there,
   get it in first (see below) — don't cite a slug that doesn't resolve.
2. Open the actual content — the TeX, or the transcribed page — and confirm the
   statement/proof you're anchoring is really there.
3. Only then write the anchor.

## Anchor forms — pick by what the source actually is

The manifest's `read` field for each entry tells you which case you're in.

- **The source has LaTeX** (arXiv e-print, an open `.tex`, etc.): read the TeX
  directly and cite the source as a whole — `\source{slug}`. Do **not** invent a
  `page-NNNN`; a TeX source has no rendered pages, so a page number would be
  fabricated. If the manifest documents stable sub-ids for the source (a section
  or label id), you may use `\source{slug:<id>}`, but only an id that exists.
- **The source is PDF-only** (no usable TeX): cite the transcribed page,
  `\source{slug:page-NNNN}`, where `page-NNNN` is a real file under
  `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` that you have read. If that page hasn't
  been transcribed yet, transcribe it first (below) — don't cite a page that
  doesn't exist on disk.

Multiple anchors may be comma-separated: `\source{slug:page-0042, other:page-0007}`.

## Getting a source into the library

Don't fetch and stash sources ad hoc. Spawn the **`reference-retriever`** subagent
(by name, through your engine's native subagent mechanism) with whatever you have
— topic, arXiv ID, DOI, title, URL, target page range. It downloads the original
(preferring TeX, keeping the PDF), verifies the file is real (not a paywall/login
page named `.pdf`), organises it under `references/<slug>/`, and registers it in
`references/manifest.yaml`. Wait for it, then cite from what it wrote.

## Extracting the LaTeX from a PDF-only source

When there is no reliable TeX and you need the actual math (to read it, or to cite
a page), **extract it with the proper tool — don't eyeball the PDF and paraphrase.**
The extraction path is the **`page-transcriber`** subagent, which renders each page
to an image and **vision-transcribes** it into one self-contained
`references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` per page.

- **Vision, never OCR.** OCR mangles math (subscripts, operators, alignment);
  reading the rendered page image with a vision model preserves it. This is a hard
  rule of the transcription flow.
- **A small vision model is usually enough.** Faithful page transcription doesn't
  need a frontier model — a cheap vision-capable model typically suffices. The
  Horizon agent chooses the model and effort at dispatch time; do not encode that
  spend policy in `config.yaml` or the descriptor.
- **Keep each call ≤5 pages.** Longer ranges lose accuracy; split a big range
  across several `page-transcriber` calls.

## Reading transcriptions correctly

- A transcribed page is `references/<slug>/tex/page-NNNN.tex` where `NNNN` is the
  **PDF page index**, which often differs from the printed page number. The
  manifest entry's `read` field records the `page_offset` and any fallback that
  actually worked — respect it when mapping "Theorem 3.4 on p. 12" to a file.
- Read the whole page file before citing it; a page can hold several results.

## The manifest at a glance

One entry per source (the `reference-retriever` owns the full schema):

```yaml
references:
  - slug: <slug>
    title: <title>
    source: <arXiv ID / DOI / URL>
    status: ok            # or: not_found
    files:
      - { path: <slug>/<slug>.pdf, format: pdf }
      - { path: <slug>/source.tex, format: tex }        # if TeX obtained
      - { path: <slug>/tex/page-0042.tex, format: tex } # if transcribed
    read: "Read TeX when present; else page anchors slug:page-NNNN. page_offset: ..."
```

If a source can't be found and verified, it's recorded `status: not_found` — treat
that as "no citation available," and write no math attributed to it.

Related skills: `blueprint-conventions` for where `\source{...}` sits among the
other blueprint annotations, and `hgraph` for how a node's `sources` feed the DAG.

232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :

235	  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)

252	/-- **The compatibility constructor from anchored refinement data** (the pre-DD-2 field
253	layout): a base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with `pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)`
254	and a comparison unit `eqn j = unit j · res (d.eqn (pt j))`. The pointwise clause
255	`eqn_rel` is derived by rewriting `d.eqn (pt j)` into `d.eqn y` through the transition
256	unit `d.ratioUnit (pt j) y` on the overlap (the `DivEq.trans` calc pattern). -/
257	def ofAnchors (D : FinCoverData C R π)
258	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
259	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
260	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
261	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
262	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
263	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
264	    DivisorAdaptation C R π d where
265	  toFinCoverData := D
266	  eqn := eqn
267	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
268	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
269	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
270	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
271	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
272	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
273	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E1
274	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
275	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
276	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E2
277	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
278	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
279	    rw [Units.val_mul]
280	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
281	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
282	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
283	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
284	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
285	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
286	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
287	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
288	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
289	            from rfl]
290	          exact E1
291	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
292	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
293	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
294	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
295	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
296	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
297	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
298	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
299	          rw [E2]
300	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
301	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
302	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
303	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
304	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
305	          rw [mul_assoc]

307	/-- The adaptation's equations are regular: at `z ∈ D(h_j)` the pointwise clause
308	`eqn_rel j z` presents the germ of `f_j` as a unit germ times the germ of `d`'s regular
309	equation at the member of `z` itself. -/
310	theorem eqn_regular (j : A.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces j) :
311	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
312	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
313	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
314	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
315	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
316	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
317	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
318	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
319	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
320	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
321	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
322	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
323	    exact h
324	  rw [hgerm]
325	  exact mul_mem
326	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
327	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
328	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))

330	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
331	
332	/-- The chart-local colength module `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`, an `R`-algebra through
333	`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra`. -/
334	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=
335	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
336	
337	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
338	two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
339	through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
340	DEFINITION. -/
341	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
342	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
343	  Ideal.span
344	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
345	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
346	
347	/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/
348	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : A.index) : Type u :=
349	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
350	
351	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength i → ovlColength i j` (restrict, then quotient;
352	the ideal of `f_i` lands in the symmetric span). -/
353	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : A.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
354	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
355	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
356	    (by
357	      intro a ha
358	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
359	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
360	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
361	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
362	          (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
363	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
364	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
365	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
366	
367	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength j → ovlColength i j`. -/
368	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : A.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
369	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
370	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
371	    (by
372	      intro a ha
373	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
374	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
375	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
376	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
377	          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
378	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
379	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
380	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
381	
382	/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
383	instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
384	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j
385	
386	/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
387	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
388	
389	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
390	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
391	  LinearMap.pi
392	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
393	
394	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
395	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
396	  LinearMap.pi
397	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
398	
399	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
400	overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
401	kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
403	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
404	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
405	
406	/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
407	the two overlap restrictions. -/
408	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
409	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
410	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
411	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
412	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
413	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
414	
415	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
416	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule

418	/-! ### The certificate -/
419	
420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
440	  flat_coker_diff :
441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
442

449	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
451	adaptation. -/
452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns

461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
465	  iseqv :=
466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩

470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/

482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :

84	/-- **The locally certified pin respects divisor equality**: the local `DivEq`s
85	transport through `divEq_pullback` (regularity along the chart immersions is free). -/
86	theorem IsLocallyCertified.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
87	    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
88	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d' := by
89	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
90	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
91	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
92	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
93	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
94	  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
95	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
96	      h _ _)⟩

98	/-- **A global certificate is a local one** (the trivial cover `g = ![1]`): the
99	certified part over `Localization.Away (1 : R)` is `mapAlg` of the family, whose
100	equations are the pulled system on the nose (`pulledEquations` IS the pullback along
101	the comparison; the regularity proofs are proof-irrelevant). -/
102	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamily.isLocallyCertified {n : ℕ}
103	    (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : IsLocallyCertified C R π n F.eqns := by
104	  refine ⟨1, fun _ => (1 : R), ?_, fun i => ?_⟩
105	  · have hrange : Set.range (fun _ : Fin 1 => (1 : R)) = {1} := Set.range_const
106	    rw [hrange, Ideal.span_singleton_one]
107	  · haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (1 : R))) :=
108	      isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (1 : R)) 1
109	    exact ⟨F.mapAlg (Localization.Away (1 : R)) n,
110	      Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _⟩

116	variable {n : ℕ} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
117	variable (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']
118	
119	/-- **The mapAlg-hreg engine** (S5b): a locally certified system has regular pulled
120	equations along the comparison of an ARBITRARY test tower `R → R'`. Regularity is
121	germ-local on the curve: the charts `Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i))` cover
122	`relCurve C R'` by open immersions; over each, the composite comparison factors
123	through the certified chart `Localization.Away (g i)`, where the certificate's
124	pullback regularity (`DivisorAdaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors`)
125	transports through the recorded `DivEq`. -/
126	theorem IsLocallyCertified.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
127	    (hloc : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d)
128	    (y z : relCurve C R') (hz : z ∈ (d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y) :
129	    ((relCurve C R').presheaf.germ ((d.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C R R')).opens y)
130	        z hz).hom (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn (relCurveMap C R R') d y)
131	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R').presheaf.stalk z) := by
132	  classical
133	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hloc
134	  -- the away charts of `R'` at the pushed cover, and their immersions
135	  haveI himm : ∀ i : ULift.{u} (Fin m),
136	      IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R'
137	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) := fun i =>
138	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R'
139	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
140	  -- the pushed family spans the unit ideal of `R'`
141	  have hspan' : Ideal.span (Set.range
142	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) = ⊤ := by
143	    have hrange : Set.range (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
144	        = algebraMap R R' '' Set.range g := by
145	      ext x
146	      constructor
147	      · rintro ⟨i, rfl⟩
148	        exact ⟨g i.down, ⟨i.down, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
149	      · rintro ⟨-, ⟨j, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
150	        exact ⟨⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
151	    rw [hrange, ← Ideal.map_span, hg, Ideal.map_top]
152	  refine Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_immersion_cover
153	    (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => relCurveMap C R'
154	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))
155	    (fun y' => exists_relCurveMap_base_eq C R'
156	      (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin m) => algebraMap R R' (g i.down))
157	      (fun i => Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) hspan' y')
158	    (relCurveMap C R R') d (fun i ζ => ?_) y z hz
159	  -- over the chart at `g i`: factor the composite through the certified localization
160	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i.down
161	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) :=
162	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i.down)) (g i.down)
163	  -- the away map `Localization.Away (g i) → Localization.Away (φ (g i))` as an
164	  -- algebra tower
165	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away (g i.down))
166	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
167	    (IsLocalization.map (M := Submonoid.powers (g i.down))
168	      (T := Submonoid.powers (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
169	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) (algebraMap R R')
170	      (by
171	        rintro x ⟨e, rfl⟩
172	        use e
173	        simp)).toAlgebra
174	  haveI : IsScalarTower R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
175	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
176	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
177	      rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, IsLocalization.map_comp,
178	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq])
179	  haveI : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (g i.down))
180	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
181	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (by
182	      rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R (Localization.Away (g i.down)),
183	        ← RingHom.comp_assoc,
184	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
185	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))),
186	        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k R
187	          (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))])
188	  -- the comparison triangle through the two factorizations of `C_{T i} → C_R`
189	  have hcomp₁ : relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
190	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
191	      ≫ relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))
192	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
193	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := Localization.Away (g i.down))
194	      (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
195	  have hcomp₂ : relCurveMap C R' (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
196	      ≫ relCurveMap C R R'
197	      = relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))) :=
198	    relCurveMap_comp (R' := R')
199	      (R'' := Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
200	  have step1 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_congr hcomp₂ d ζ
201	  have step2 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_comp hcomp₁ d
202	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
203	      (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i.down))) d) ζ
204	  have hfinal := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_self_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_divEq
205	    (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
206	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))) hGdiv ζ
207	    (G.adaptation.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors
208	      (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down)))
209	      G.certified.projective_colength ζ ζ
210	      ((G.eqns.cover.pullback (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away (g i.down))
211	        (Localization.Away (algebraMap R R' (g i.down))))).mem_opens ζ))
212	  exact ((step1.trans step2).symm ▸ hfinal)
213	
214	end MapAlgHreg

221	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on locally certified systems (Addendum 2's mirror of
222	`divFamSetoid`): the underlying local-equation systems cut the same divisor; the local
223	certificates are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
224	def divFamZarSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
225	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} where
226	  r d₁ d₂ := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁.1 d₂.1
227	  iseqv :=
228	    ⟨fun d => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl d.1,
229	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
230	
231	/-- **The locally certified divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`**
232	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): locally certified local-equation systems of
233	degree `n` up to divisor equality. This is the carrier on which the divisor functor is
234	a Zariski sheaf — the globally certified `DivFam` remains the building block. -/
235	def DivFamZar : Type u := Quotient (divFamZarSetoid C R π n)
236	
237	namespace DivFamZar
238	
239	variable {C R π n}
240	
241	/-- The class of a locally certified system. -/
242	def mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) :
243	    DivFamZar C R π n :=
244	  Quotient.mk (divFamZarSetoid C R π n) ⟨d, hd⟩
245	
246	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {d₁ d₂ : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
247	    {h₁ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₁} {h₂ : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d₂} :
248	    mk d₁ h₁ = mk d₂ h₂ ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d₁ d₂ :=
249	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamZarSetoid C R π n)
250	
251	/-- **The Picard class of a locally certified divisor class** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on
252	the quotient by `picClass_eq_of_divEq`. -/
253	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFamZar C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
254	  Quotient.lift
255	    (fun d : {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations // IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} =>
256	      d.1.picClass)
257	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
258	
259	@[simp]
260	lemma picClass_mk (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
261	    (hd : IsLocallyCertified C R π n d) : picClass (mk d hd) = d.picClass :=
262	  rfl
263	
264	end DivFamZar

266	variable {C R π n}

268	/-- **The comparison from the globally certified value**: a certified family is
269	locally certified (trivial cover), and divisor equality is the relation on both
270	sides. Over a field the two notions agree; over a general base `toZar` is the
271	sheafification-of-value comparison. -/
272	def DivFam.toZar : DivFam C R π n → DivFamZar C R π n :=
273	  Quotient.lift
274	    (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n =>
275	      DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified)
276	    (fun _ _ h => DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr h)
277	
278	@[simp]
279	lemma DivFam.toZar_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
280	    (DivFam.mk F).toZar = DivFamZar.mk F.eqns F.isLocallyCertified :=
281	  rfl

283	/-- The Picard class factors through `toZar`. -/
284	@[simp]
285	lemma DivFamZar.picClass_toZar (F : DivFam C R π n) :
286	    F.toZar.picClass = F.picClass := by
287	  induction F using Quotient.inductionOn with
288	  | h F => rfl
